question.text: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mi>x</mi></mfenced></math> satisfies the differential equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mn>1</mn></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, then <math><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to

solution.text:
The given differential equation is a linear differential equation.

Integrating factor =e∫2x1+x2dx=1+x2
The solution of the differential equation is y1+x2=∫3x2dx=x3+C

∵y1=1⇒C=1
Hence, y=fx=x3+1x2+1

So, f2=95=1.8
